findings.gap: No prescribed same-title two-record witness establishes that title is a display name rather than a uniqueness/key constraint. S21 uses different Alpha/Beta titles; S23 verifies rename/update under one identity. Other fixture titles are distinct or left to the judge, with no required collision.
findings.counterexample: Use stable integer identities and otherwise correct revisions/history, but add UNIQUE(title) and refuse New/Save whenever another record already has that title. All specified distinct-title create/update flows can pass, while two legitimate New drafts both titled Sketch cannot become separate records. Alternatively a title-based upsert can overwrite the first record only on duplicate-title creation without affecting any required S21/S23 observation.
findings.fix: In S21 create two New drafts with the same nonempty title and distinct source/filenames; require different identities, load both, and update one while the other remains unchanged. Keep the operation outcome independently scored.

findings.gap: The retry scenario does not require a fresh deliberate attempt to the same historical target to commit another new revision. Step 5 replays the original token correctly; step 5a may choose another target and only compares retry with its captured successful response/no second write. It never explicitly checks that the new deliberate attempt first advanced the preceding head and added exactly one revision. The Save/restore race does not guarantee a restore win or reuse of a previously restored target.
findings.counterexample: An implementation caches original attempt results correctly for retry/restart, rejects fresh stale bases, but after a valid current-base check also deduplicates restores by (snippet ID, target snapshot). The first restore of revision A commits R4; a later Save commits R5. A deliberate new attempt to restore A incorrectly returns cached R4 and leaves R5 current. Existing exact-token retries still work. Step 5a can choose B (as the supplied scripted proof actually did), so both its fresh restore and lost-reply retry succeed; the duplicate-target defect remains unexercised. Even selecting A lacks an explicit pre-attempt-head/new-history assertion in step 5a.
findings.fix: After a successful restore and newer Save, deliberately restore the same old target with a fresh attempt identity and require a new advanced head plus exactly one new snapshot; replay that second attempt and require no further change. Reuse the lost-reply trial if desired, but first prove its initial commit against pre-attempt state.

findings.gap: The no-execution-on-opening promise is exercised only during genuinely queued-edit cancellation. There is no opening of a saved record or New with Auto-run enabled after the queue has drained.
findings.counterexample: A source-loading handler suppresses its programmatic source change only when cancelPending() finds an existing timer; otherwise the normal source-change effect schedules Auto-run. It passes S17 step 7 because both New/load trials deliberately have pending timers, and passes save/load/history scenarios because Auto-run is off there. A user who waits for Auto-run to complete and then opens another saved snippet gets an unwanted execution, contrary to the explicit merely-opening rule.
findings.fix: Extend the shared S17 evidence with an enabled-but-idle load and New after an observed automatic completion; wait the measured debounce margin without edit/Run and require no new execution, then positively prove a later edit still runs.

conforming_alternative_challenge: Checked a conforming app using opaque/nonconsecutive revision IDs, SSR library responses, automatic lost-reply retry, a static rollback picture, alternate control names and standard editor escape. Current prompts explicitly accept these alternatives; no new row-26 false-failure finding from them. Fixes above should not require numeric +1 revisions, fixed routes, manual Retry after automatic recovery, or source inspection.
shared_policy_note: Express/SQLite/no-external-backend mandates are inherited verbatim in substance from the frozen template. They cannot be proved by these browser criteria (Constraints:29 expressly says so). Preserve shared policy and record this measurement boundary; do not add prohibited source reading or mislabel shared policy as a task-added defect.
